domain: Moral Philosophy / Historical Ethics / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Spartan infant exposure as a test case for personhood-boundary kernel contestation across time. Examines whether the hillside-exposure reading (infanticide as legitimate population control) represents a dropped reading from a shared kernel or exit from the moral possibility space entirely. Tests whether moral-standing boundaries are contested kernels with multiple live readings or historical succession of incommensurable frameworks.

key_entities: Spartan state (authority structure enforcing exposure practice)
Gerousia (council of elders adjudicating infant fitness)
key_tensions: State eugenic interest vs individual infant life (Spartan practice vs modern rights)
Fitness-based personhood vs birth-based personhood (exposure reading vs modern reading)
Historical moral possibility vs contemporary moral necessity (path-naturalization question)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood-boundary kernel: what entities possess moral standing requiring protection from killing
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Varies by reading: Spartan = state eugenic authority; modern = rights-based constitutional/philosophical consensus

readings.commitment: Personhood contingent on demonstrated fitness; pre-fitness entities lack moral standing
readings.authority_grounding: State eugenic interest; collective survival priority over individual life
readings.expected_structural_delta: Infants enter victim set only after passing fitness test; state authority to exclude pre-test entities from moral community

readings.commitment: Personhood begins at birth; all born humans possess moral standing
readings.authority_grounding: Rights-based framework; inherent dignity independent of capacity
readings.expected_structural_delta: All born infants in victim set; killing any born human is homicide; no state authority to exclude

readings.commitment: Personhood grounded in potential for rational agency; severely disabled infants may lack standing
readings.expected_structural_delta: Victim set excludes entities without potential for personhood-relevant capacities; parental/medical authority to make exclusion judgments

axiom_contradictions.basis: No framework can simultaneously hold that personhood is contingent on demonstrated fitness AND that all born humans inherently possess it. Accepting birth-threshold axiom requires rejecting fitness-contingency as a legitimate criterion.

No framework can hold both that birth confers inviolable moral standing AND that lack of potential for rational agency permits exclusion. Birth-threshold treats birth as sufficient; potential-based treats it as insufficient without capacity.

omegas.description: Core uncertainty: Is personhood-boundary a contested kernel with multiple live readings, or historical succession of incommensurable frameworks? If succession, fitness-contingent reading did not 'drop' from kernel but exited moral possibility space entirely. If kernel, modern consensus suppresses a reading that remains structurally available.

Does contemporary moral philosophy treat birth-threshold as discovered necessity or naturalized contingency? If naturalized, the 'modern window' is itself a reading-suppression mechanism. If necessity, Spartan practice was moral error, not alternative reading.
omegas.source: Deferred axis path_naturalization_mechanism + Dark Matter Probe 3

omegas.description: Is fitness-contingent reading genuinely unavailable from modern frameworks, or merely suppressed? Singer/McMahan potential-based reading demonstrates partial structural availability. Question: does taboo against infanticide reflect reasoned rejection or availability cascade?
